subject: EdgeByte: reserve slab + headroom multipliers for Dedicated commit
body:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Nguyen <clara@edgebyte.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: EdgeByte: reserve slab + headroom multipliers for Dedicated commit

Hi Clara — thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a short proposal for how we would structure the Dedicated commit so EdgeByte can have predictable baseline capacity while also having a safe, billable burst envelope for marketing spikes and batched training jobs. See attached high-level plan (EdgeByte_MA_plan_v2.pdf) and the raw burst calcs (gpu_burst_calcs.xlsx).

Summary proposal (short):
- Reserve slab: 12 A100-80GB equivalents dedicated to EdgeByte (baseline commit).
- Headroom multipliers: allow 1.5x short-term burst above slab for up to 3 minutes per request spike, and 2.5x for scheduled batch windows (max 60 minutes/day).
- Autoscale policy: continuous autoscaler up to 3x baseline with cooldown of 90s for scale-up and 10m for scale-down.
- Billing: baseline charged at committed rate; bursts billed at on-demand per-GPU minute; we apply a 25% burst discount in year 1.

Questions for you: does the 12 A100 baseline sound right given your SLOs? Do you want a higher short-term multiplier for campaign launches?

Thanks,
Dylan
--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D +1 415-555-0142


From: Clara Nguyen <clara@edgebyte.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@edgebyte.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: EdgeByte: reserve slab + headroom multipliers for Dedicated commit

Thanks Dylan — attaching our rough traffic heatmap in a follow-up (will send separately). Quick responses:
- 12 A100 baseline is close but we typically run a 20% safety buffer on top of steady-state; can we make baseline 14?
- For marketing spikes we need at least 2x for the first 10 minutes of a campaign launch.
- For scheduled batches, 3x for up to 2 hours is ideal (we have nightly model refresh runs).

If those are doable, we can move forward on the term sheet.

-Clara
Head of ML Ops | EdgeByte


From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Clara Nguyen <clara@edgebyte.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: EdgeByte: reserve slab + headroom multipliers for Dedicated commit

On Fri, 12 Feb 2027 at 11:03 AM Clara Nguyen <clara@edgebyte.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Dylan — attaching our rough traffic heatmap in a follow-up (will send separately). Quick responses:
> - 12 A100 baseline is close but we typically run a 20% safety buffer on top of steady-state; can we make baseline 14?
> - For marketing spikes we need at least 2x for the first 10 minutes of a campaign launch.
> - For scheduled batches, 3x for up to 2 hours is ideal (we have nightly model refresh runs).

Hi Clara — thanks for the details. A couple of technical clarifications from the runtime side to align expectations before we finalize: 
- Hardware mix: baseline committed capacity will be placed on A100 equivalents by default; we can auto-fallback to H100 variants for burst if you want higher perf but note H100 pricing is ~30% higher for on-demand bursts.
- Burst safety: to avoid noisy-neighbor risks we recommend capping instantaneous cluster-wide headroom at 2.5x of baseline for uncontrolled ad-hoc spikes; for scheduled batch windows we can allow up to 3x under a controlled policy (jobs must be tagged as SCHEDULED_BATCH).
- Pre-warm & cold-start: if you expect sudden short bursts (<120s) for low-latency web traffic, add a tiny prefix cache (2-3 tokens warmers per model) otherwise first requests may see +200ms cold overhead during scaling.
- Autoscaler tuning suggestion: scale-up multiplier triggers at 70% aggregate GPU utilization and scale-down when sustained under 30% for the cooldown period. Keep scale-down cooldown at 10 minutes to avoid churn.

I'll update the attached spreadsheet with per-GPU-minute cost delta (A100 vs H100 vs L4) and a few example billings for the patterns you listed.

Regards,
Marissa
Director, Dedicated Systems | Redwood Inference


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Nguyen <clara@edgebyte.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: EdgeByte: reserve slab + headroom multipliers for Dedicated commit

Clara — per Marissa's notes, here's an updated proposal that tries to meet EdgeByte's needs while keeping cost predictability: 
- Baseline commit: 14 A100-equivalent GPUs (committed).
- Ad-hoc web spike headroom: 2x baseline allowed for up to 15 minutes, per-occurrence, with 30m global cool-off for repeated bursts.
- Scheduled batch windows: up to 3x baseline for up to 2 hours nightly when jobs are flagged SCHEDULED_BATCH.
- Autoscaler: scale-up at 70% util (2x trigger), scale-down after 10m below 30% util; scale-up cooldown 90s.
- Billing: baseline at committed rate; ad-hoc burst (2x) billed per-minute at on-demand with a 20% volume discount if monthly burst minutes > 50,000. Scheduled batch burst billed similarly but invoiced on the committed account with monthly reconciliation.

If that sounds good, I'll draft term sheet language and work with Legal/Finance to add the burst discount and the SCHEDULED_BATCH tagging requirement.

Next steps:
- Clara: confirm acceptance of baseline = 14 and the burst windows above.
- Lauren: can you own drafting the revenue-side wording for monthly reconciliation and burst discount?
- Marissa: please attach the updated cost tab so Clara can see example invoices.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference


From: Clara Nguyen <clara@edgebyte.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@edgebyte.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EdgeByte: reserve slab + headroom multipliers for Dedicated commit

Thanks all — that structure is acceptable. We formally accept baseline = 14 and the scheduled batch windows as described. A couple clarifications for the contract:
- Please include a clause that scheduled batch windows must be declared 24 hours in advance in the console or via API; ad-hoc marketing bursts remain unrestricted but subject to the 30m global cool-off.
- We agree to the monthly reconciliation model for scheduled batches.
- Confirmed deal id EB-7890.

We can proceed to term sheet.

Best,
Clara
Head of ML Ops | EdgeByte

Attachments: EdgeByte_MA_plan_v2.pdf, gpu_burst_calcs.xlsx
